The '''Belcantese Language Institute''' was the postwar language authority created by the [[Language Restoration Act of 1950]]. It oversaw restoration and standardization of the [[Belcantese Language]] after more than five decades of Vesperan occupation.

== Work ==

The institute developed grammar standards, dictionaries, education guidance, administrative terminology, and modern vocabulary for reconstruction. It also helped collect texts preserved by the [[Belcantese Cultural Resistance]], including material connected to the [[Resistance Songbook]].

== Role In State-Building ==

Language policy was part of postwar state-building. The institute helped make Belcantese usable in courts, schools, public administration, diplomatic correspondence, and national cultural institutions.

== Canon Note ==

Source material cites a 1995 grammar from the institute. This draft covers the institution through 1994 and treats the 1995 reference as immediate post-window evidence to be used in a later pass.
